corrections.claim: Penoyre et al. 2022 propose RUWE 1.25 as the EDR3 binarity threshold.
corrections.correction: Penoyre et al. 2022 (arXiv:2202.06963) renormalise RUWE locally (LUWE) and use LUWE > 2; a flat 1.25 cut circulates in secondary literature but is not in their abstract. Castro-Ginard et al. 2024 (A&A, doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202450172) instead publish sky-position-dependent RUWE thresholds (GaiaUnlimited package). Use RUWE > 1.4 (Lindegren 2018) as the hard flag and treat 1.0-1.4 as 'no evidence' per Stassun & Torres 2021.
corrections.evidence: WebFetch of arXiv:2202.06963 abstract ('We use the simple criterion of LUWE>2'); WebSearch results for Castro-Ginard 2024.

additions: The bright 7.1" neighbour KIC 5689116 / Gaia DR3 2103792427466721792 (the star whose TPF hosts the KBONUS extraction) has Gaia DR3 RUWE 8.73, astrometric_excess_noise 2.42 mas (sig 976) and parallax 0.30 ± 0.23 mas [run]. The neighbour is itself a strong astrometric-binary / disturbed-solution candidate. Kuber's neighbour light-curve (24 ± 41 ppm) and centroid tests still argue the dip is not on it, but the playbook must run RUWE/AEN/NSS checks on every Gaia source inside the aperture (not just the target), and a MOLUSC/companion argument for the neighbour-hosted-EB branch should use this value. ExoFOP's nearby-target list (download_nearbytarget.php?id=120686465) shows the neighbour without a distance for the same reason.

MAST TESS SPOC TCE bulk CSVs (https://archive.stsci.edu/missions/tess/catalogs/tce/, files tess<ts>-s<start>-s<stop>_dvr-tcestats.csv, single sectors 1-107 and multi-sector bundles) carry tce_period, tce_time0bt, tce_depth, tce_max_mult_ev, tce_ntoi, tce_dicco_msky, tce_ditco_msky, tce_cap_stat/tce_hap_stat (ghost), boot_fap, tce_albedo_stat etc. [run]. Use them (plus the TESS-SPOC HLSP FFI DV products, available from Sector 36, multi-sector from Sector 56, for T<=13.5 targets) to answer 'was this ever a TCE' for TESS — the Exoplanet Archive only hosts TOIs, not TCEs, for TESS.

Standard Kepler light-curve files contain MOM_CENTR1/2 (flux-weighted) and PSF_CENTR1/2 centroid columns plus POS_CORR1/2 and header keywords CROWDSAP, FLFRCSAP, MODULE/OUTPUT/CHANNEL/SKYGROUP [run on kplr005689116 Q1: CROWDSAP 0.9469, FLFRCSAP 0.8176, channel 6, skygroup 50]. For any KBONUS candidate, the TPF owner's own LC file gives an independent, pipeline-produced flux-weighted centroid series to fold at the candidate ephemeris — a cheaper first pass than re-deriving centroids from TPFs.

KBONUS light-curve file anatomy for dilution/aperture modelling [run]: PRIMARY header has TPFORG (= KIC of the originating TPF, 5689116 here), KEPLERID, GAIAID; LIGHTCURVE_STITCHED has TIME, CADENCENO, QUARTER, FLUX (PSF), SAP_FLUX, PSF_FLAT_FLUX, SAP_QUALITY, FLATTEN_MASK; each LIGHTCURVE_Qn carries per-quarter PSFFRAC, CROWDSAP, FLFRCSAP, PERTRATI, PERTSTD, MODULE, OUTPUT, CHANNEL and an APERTURE_Qn image (5x4 or 5x5 px). KIC 5689121 has 13 quarters (Q1-4, 6-8, 10-12, 14-16), matching the 13 TPFs of KIC 5689116 (keplerstellar st_quarters '11110111011101110'). lightkurve search with author='KBONUS-BKG' returns both the target's and the neighbour's KBONUS products, so the neighbour-light-curve test is one extra download.

Gaia colour-magnitude over-luminosity is a cheap unresolved-binary test the brief omits: an equal-brightness companion lifts a star ~0.75 mag above the single-star main sequence at its BP-RP; compare the target's absolute G (from the Gaia parallax) with an empirical M-dwarf sequence (e.g. the method of arXiv:2602.20096, which identified 21,864 unresolved low-mass binaries this way). It constrains exactly the STP/PTP scenarios that dominate Kuber's FPP.

Ephemeris-uncertainty propagation should be an explicit, logged number: σ_T(N) = sqrt(σ_T0² + N²σ_P²). For P = 13.769448 ± 0.000065 d, T0 = 2455630.245431 ± 0.0020, N = 430 cycles to 2027-06-01 gives σ_T = 40.3 min [run], confirming Kuber's '~40 min by 2027'. Any follow-up window must also carry the barycentric correction for the observatory and the Gaia proper motion for acquisition.

TRICERATOPS 1.1.0 now exposes a `FPP_degenerate` attribute and emits a RuntimeWarning when every MC draw is geometrically invalid ('FPP=1.0 reflects a failed computation, not a confident false positive'); always check it, and check that `T.probs` has all 15 target rows (D/B scenarios silently dropped when the field-star query fails). Also run FPP across the method-dependent depth range (Kuber: 1,830-2,430 ppm) since FPP is depth-sensitive.

The Exoplanet Archive KOI column docs define the four FP flags and the centroid columns: koi_dicco_msky (difference-image PRF centroid vs out-of-transit centroid, arcsec), koi_dikco_msky (vs KIC position), koi_fwm_stat_sig (flux-weighted offset significance, %), koi_comment (Robovetter minor flags), koi_time0bk offset 2,454,833.0; use these columns, not just dispositions, when screening nearby KOIs as contamination parents.

Guerrero 2021 CTOI mechanics worth copying into the plan: 'ExoFOP emphasizes CTOIs should only be reported if there is no TOI with the same period'; of 169 prime-mission promoted CTOIs, 106 were TCEs 'mistakenly ruled out in pre-vetting triage'; CTOIs with no TCE and no QLP/SPOC products 'would need to be recovered manually in a reprocessing step'; TOI list updated twice daily on ExoFOP, monthly static copy at MAST.

Kostov et al. 2025 (TESS Ten Thousand) photocentre rule, now verified: PRF fit and Gaussian fit to each difference image, average adopted, offset threshold 0.2 px (≈4"); catalogue is 'machine-readable online supplement' (Table 3), not on VizieR as of today.

TESS-SPOC HLSP (archive.stsci.edu/hlsp/tess-spoc) runs planet searches on FFI targets with T <= 13.5 (plus H <= 10 and d < 100 pc) since May 2021, producing DV products for targets with TCEs (single-sector from S36, multi-sector from S56). This is the primary source behind Chopra's corrected 'SPOC has searched FFI light curves since 2021' and should be queried before any 'never searched' statement.

DR25 Robovetter Table 4 ships three threshold sets (DR25, 'High C' completeness-optimised, 'High R' reliability-optimised); for a small-sample candidate hunt the High-R column (e.g. MS1 DV -1.0, SES/MES 0.75, Chases 0.55, LPP 2.7) is the conservative choice to pre-register.
